answer: The inspector counts the rivets of every span and writes the number in his book, so the bridge is proved sound span by span. A dawn span claimed as counted fails the book: the rivets must be the inspector's own tally at the raven of the span, and a span never counted shows rust the book never mentions. Buying a false rivet count costs 21,600 in bribes to the inspector and fees to the riveting gang, and the whisper entry in the book is read at every flood, so a bridge whose spans were never counted is closed to traffic.
